controls.title: Representations of Authorized Network Communication and Data Flows are Maintained
controls.intent: Ensure that authorized network communications and internal and external network data flows are defined and maintained to support secure network operation and risk management.
controls.summary: Authorized network communications and data flows should be documented and reflected in the deployed network architecture. Unexpected network communication may indicate that implemented communication paths deviate from the intended design.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA provides objective technical evidence that observed network communication paths are consistent with the intended segmentation policy by validating actual reachability against the authorized communication model.
expected_evidence: Observed communication inconsistent with the authorized communication model
assessment_notes: Unexpected communication provides objective technical evidence that implemented communication paths differ from those intended by the network architecture.
NSSA validates observable communication behaviour rather than network documentation.
limitations: Cannot determine whether architectural documentation exists or is maintained.
Cannot assess business-level data flow documentation.
Only evaluates network communication behaviour against the intended segmentation policy.

controls.title: Access Permissions, Entitlements, and Authorizations are Defined, Managed, Enforced, and Reviewed
controls.intent: Ensure that access permissions enforce least privilege by allowing only authorized communications between systems and network segments.
controls.summary: Access to network-accessible systems should only be permitted from authorized sources according to defined authorization policies. Unexpected communication may indicate ineffective enforcement of network-level access restrictions.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA provides objective technical evidence that network-level authorization policies are effectively enforced by validating observed communication against the intended segmentation policy.
expected_evidence: Unauthorized host reaches a protected system
assessment_notes: Unexpected communication provides objective technical evidence that network-level authorization policies are not being enforced as intended.
NSSA evaluates network authorization rather than user identities or application authorization.
limitations: Cannot assess identity management, authentication or user permissions.

controls.title: Configuration Management Practices are Established and Applied
controls.intent: Ensure that technology platforms are configured so that deployed systems consistently enforce the intended security policy.
controls.summary: Technology platforms should consistently enforce the intended security policy. Unexpected network reachability may indicate that platform configurations are not producing the expected security behaviour.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA provides objective technical evidence that deployed configurations effectively enforce the intended segmentation policy by validating observed communication behaviour.
expected_evidence: Communication inconsistent with the intended policy
assessment_notes: Observed communication inconsistent with policy provides objective technical evidence that deployed configurations are not enforcing the intended restrictions.
NSSA evaluates externally observable behaviour rather than platform configuration settings.
limitations: Cannot inspect operating system, firewall or network device configurations.
Cannot determine which configuration caused the observed behaviour.
Does not assess configuration management processes.

controls.title: Networks and Environments are Protected from Unauthorized Logical Access and Usage
controls.intent: Ensure that networks and network environments prevent unauthorized logical communications and enforce the intended security boundaries.
controls.summary: Networks should only permit authorized logical communications. Unauthorized communication between systems or network segments indicates that logical access controls are not effectively enforced.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA directly validates whether deployed network segmentation and logical access controls effectively prevent unauthorized communication by comparing observed reachability with the intended segmentation policy.
assessment_notes: Observed unauthorized communication provides objective technical evidence that logical access protections are not effectively enforcing the intended network security architecture.
NSSA evaluates the effectiveness of logical access protection through observable network behaviour.
limitations: Cannot determine which security technology enforces logical access restrictions.
Cannot inspect firewall rules, ACLs or device configurations.
Does not evaluate physical access controls.
